metadata.title: Clean Grid Penetration vs. Industrial Power Costs
metadata.visual_form: Connected Animated Scatterplot with Localized Time Vector Trails

events.label: Wind and solar reach 3.5% of US power
COVID lowers demand; wind and solar hit 13.5%
Natural gas spike lifts factory power prices
Record: wind and solar supply 24.3% of US power

explanation.summary: Wind and solar went from almost nothing to about a fifth of US electricity. At the same time, the wholesale price of electricity for factories kept rising. More clean power has not, by itself, made industrial power cheaper; fuel prices and grid costs still matter.
explanation.methodology: Wind plus solar share of total US electricity generation, all sectors, from EIA Form 923 data (EIA API). Industrial power price is the BLS Producer Price Index for industrial electric power (WPU0543). Both series rise over time, so their high correlation mostly reflects a shared trend, not cause and effect.

key_findings.title: 2012: Wind Takes Off
key_findings.description: Wind and solar supplied 3.5% of US electricity, up from 0.3% in 2005, as wind farms spread across Texas and the Plains.
key_findings.significance: A tenfold rise in seven years.

key_findings.title: August 2022: Gas Prices Push Power Costs Up
key_findings.description: Natural gas prices spiked after the invasion of Ukraine. The factory power price index reached 301, up from 233 in early 2020.
key_findings.significance: Gas plants often set the price of power, so gas price shocks reach factories.

key_findings.title: April 2026: A New Record
key_findings.description: Wind and solar supplied 24.3% of US electricity in April 2026, the highest month on record. Spring is when wind is strong, sun is rising and demand is low.
key_findings.significance: Clean power's share keeps climbing, but factory power prices also hit a record (344) in July 2026.
